exposure: mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal birth, assisted vaginal birth, induced vaginal birth, emergency cesarean section, planned cesarean section, cesarean section after induction)
cohort: The study included 10,507 singleton mothers from the Millennium Cohort Study.
finding: The study found an association between induction of labor and an increased risk of long-term depression/severe anxiety by 14 years postpartum, but no significant association for other modes of birth.
mod_finding: Induction of labor was associated with an increased risk of long-term depression/severe anxiety by 14 years postpartum, but other modes of birth showed no significant association.
